title: User econ flows for multi-QoS responses (draft)
content:
Context / problem statement:

We need a lightweight, customer-configurable way to trade latency, cost, and fidelity per request surface. Many customers want predictable unit economics for different classes of requests (search, chat assistant, batch enrichment) and a simple UX to express: fast cheap, balanced, and high-fidelity. Current controls (model selection + quantization presets + routing policies) are powerful but fragmented. Idea: expose a Multi-QoS response layer that maps a named QoS tier to a bundle of runtime controls (model family, quantization level, batching patience, fallback policy, cache TTL).

Goal for this doc: sketch a minimum viable product (MVP) that productizes the mapping, UX, API, and metrics to allow engineering teams and product owners to adopt QoS tiers quickly. This is a personal scratchpad — high-level ideas, sample API sketches, user stories, and a rough rollout plan.

1) Proposed concept

- QoS Tier: a named policy (e.g., "fast", "balanced", "careful") that bundles runtime knobs.
- Each tier contains: model_variant, max_latency_ms, batching_strategy (aggressiveness), kv_cache_policy (enabled, ttl), quantization_profile, fallback_chain (ordered list), preempt_priority (for scheduling), cost_multiplier_hint (display-only for billing UX).
- Platform will evaluate tiers for feasibility per request (region, authorized models, customer entitlements) and either accept, substitute a compatible variant, or return a clear error.

2) MVP surface (what to build first)

- Console: Tier editor (create, edit, clone), tier preview showing estimated p50/p95 latency and token cost for a representative prompt shape.
- API: support passing tier_id on generation requests (hosted API + SDK). Default fallback to customer default tier.
- Server-side: translation layer that converts tier into runtime routing + kernel selection hints. Metrics emitted at request-level: chosen_model, chosen_quant, effective_latency_ms, cost_estimate_tokens, tier_requested, tier_applied, fallback_reason.

3) Example API sketch (rough)

POST /v1/generate
headers: Authorization: Bearer ...
body: {"model": "auto", "tier": "tier_fast", "prompt": "Summarize...", "max_tokens": 256}

Server semantics: if tier specified, map to candidate model list. Validate against customer entitlements. Attach telemetry tags. If model "auto", allow tier to pick default family.

4) UX notes / console flows

- Onboarding wizard: show 3 starter tiers with cards (fast/balanced/accurate) and sample prompts with cost/latency estimates.
- Per-route override: allow routes (API keys, endpoints) to pin tier defaults.
- Visualize: per-tier SLOs (p50/p95), cost per 1K tokens, fallback rate.

5) User stories

- As an application engineer, I want to create a "fast" tier that prioritizes low latency so that our chat UI feels snappy for discovery queries.
- As an ML platform engineer, I want to measure how often the "accurate" tier falls back to a larger model so we can tune rollout thresholds.
- As a product manager, I want a simple billing estimate that shows how different QoS mixes change monthly spend for a given traffic profile.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):

- Console: can create/clone/edit/delete tiers and set basic knobs (model family, max_latency_ms, quantization_profile).
- API: requests accept a tier id and return which tier was applied and any fallbacks.
- Observability: per-tier metrics exist and get visualized in a simple dashboard.

6) Metrics to track

- per-tier request count, p50/p95 latency, token cost estimate, fallback_rate, successful_apply_rate (requested vs applied), error_rate, model-switch-events.
- Business metrics: avg cost per 1k tokens by tier, aggregate spend delta vs baseline.

7) Experiments / rollout plan

Phase A (internal Beta)
- Limit to a small set of customers on hosted with high telemetry instrumentation.
- Run A/B: default routing vs tier-enforced routing for a subset of routes. Measure latency, cost, user-facing error/blips.

Phase B (public Beta)
- Expose tier editor in console, allow self-serve. Default starter tiers. Add billing estimates.

Phase C (GA)
- Support Dedicated and Private: ensure tier runtime translation works with reserved capacity and on-prem kernel variations. Add RBAC for tier creation.

8) Implementation notes / risks

- Mapping to actual kernel choices is nontrivial: we will need a capability table per deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private) that lists supported quant profiles and compatible fallback models.
- Cost estimate accuracy: early estimates will be heuristics (tokens * model_unit_cost * multiplier). Must avoid misleading customers.
- Race between batching and latency SLOs: aggressive batching reduces cost but may violate max_latency_ms; need to encode patience windows.

9) Open questions / TODOs

- How to express multi-stage fallbacks (e.g., try quantized Llama2 -> fallback to full float Llama2 -> fallback to gpt-like family)? Represent as ordered list with hard latency caps?
- Billing model: should tier metadata be purely a routing hint (and billing shows actual used model) or should we reserve a priced tier that bills based on tier chosen regardless of final model? (billing/finance input needed).
- UX: should console show simulated p50/p95 using synthetic workload or sample of customer traffic? (privacy concerns).
- Metrics: add "tier-health" alerting when fallback_rate > X% for > N minutes. Default thresholds?

10) Rough milestones (2-week sprint cadence)

Sprint 1: proto schema + server-side translator + minimal telemetry tags.
Sprint 2: console prototype (tier create/edit) + API field parsing + test harness.
Sprint 3: internal beta with 3 pilot customers + telemetry dashboards.

Notes / random ideas to revisit:
- Consider a "credit" abstraction: each request consumes credits based on tier and tokens; customers pre-buy credits for cheaper committed pricing. Could become Dedicated-like economics for hosted customers.
- Expose a lightweight simulator in console: drop in sample prompt shapes and simulate percentile latencies and spend.
- Integrate with Optimize recommendations: suggest tier changes per-route based on observed cost/latency tradeoffs.

References and links:
- Related jira: INF-2418 (QoS tiers research)
- Past notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IN/Response+Tiers+Research+Notes

Immediate next actions (me):
- Draft short RFC to share with infra and finance (goal: align on billing semantics).
- Spike a tiny server translator (map tier -> model list) and push telemetry flags.
- Book quick sync with Mika and Sam to test console mockups.

End of draft.
